statement: A prior worker on lane e-pack-frontend-react wrote a complete, correct rule impl (crates/enforcer-lang-ts/src/rules/frontend_react.rs, 13 FE-* Validator impls) plus all 14 rule-id fixture dirs (28 fail/pass fixture files) in a sibling worktree (agent-adc90ec4356c7f56f) but died at session-limit before: (1) adding `pub mod frontend_react;` to crates/enforcer-lang-ts/src/rules/mod.rs, (2) copying the fixtures into the live worktree's tests/ tree, and (3) authoring the enforcer-rules rule-record catalog (rules/frontend-react.json). The salvage was a pure copy-and-wire: no line of the rule impl or any fixture needed rewriting.
why: Confirms the workpack's premise (a dead worker's WRITTEN-but-unwired output is safely reusable) held exactly as described; worth recording because it validates the salvage-then-wire workflow as a viable recovery pattern for future session-limit deaths on other lanes.
howToApply: When resuming a lane marked as salvage-from-a-dead-worker, verify the salvage source builds against the CURRENT base FIRST (cargo build -p <crate> after copying, before writing any registry/catalog wiring) — this one compiled clean with zero API drift on first try, which is not guaranteed and should always be checked, not assumed.

statement: No API drift was found between the salvaged frontend_react.rs (written against an older rust-build tip) and the current base: `enforcer_validator::validator::{ValidationInput, Validator}`, `enforcer_domain::findings::Finding`, `enforcer_domain::ids::RuleId`, `enforcer_domain::severity::Severity`, and `enforcer_validator::harness::run_fixture_parity` all matched exactly. `cargo build -p enforcer-lang-ts` succeeded on the very first attempt after copying the file in unmodified plus the mod.rs one-line registration.
why: Rules out a base-drift blocker the workpack briefing explicitly warned about ("the salvage was written on an older base ... adapt the rule impl to the CURRENT trait signatures") — no adaptation was needed for this lane, so future readers should not assume drift-fixing time is required by default.
howToApply: Do not pre-emptively rewrite salvaged rule impls to match a suspected API change; build first, and only patch the specific compile errors that surface (there were none here).

evidence.ref: cargo build -p enforcer-lang-ts clean on first attempt post-copy

statement: The salvaged frontend_react.rs's shared `finding()` helper took 7 positional args (rule_id, severity, title, detail, input, line, snippet), which fails `clippy::too_many_arguments` (max 5) under `-D warnings`. No prior lang-pack module in this codebase carries a `#[allow(clippy::...)]` escape hatch anywhere, so the fix was a refactor (bundle severity/title/detail/line/snippet into a local `FindingSpec<'a>` struct, reducing `finding()` to 3 args: rule_id, input, spec) rather than a lint suppression, matching the workspace's no-waiver clippy posture.
why: This is exactly the kind of small-but-easy-to-miss gate failure the workpack's dogfood step (cargo clippy -D warnings after green tests) is designed to catch; a worker who skips the clippy pass because tests are green would ship a lane that fails CI on lint alone.
howToApply: When a shared `finding`/`build_finding`-style helper in a new lang-pack module needs more than 4-5 parameters, bundle the Finding-shape fields (severity/title/detail/line/snippet) into a local params struct instead of reaching for `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` — this codebase has zero clippy-allow precedent anywhere in enforcer-lang-ts/enforcer-lang-common, so refactor-not-suppress is the house style.

evidence.ref: cargo clippy -p enforcer-lang-ts -- -D warnings failed with clippy::too_many_arguments on frontend_react.rs:44 (finding fn), fixed via FindingSpec struct, then passed clean

statement: Authored crates/enforcer-rules/rules/frontend-react.json (13 records, 12 T1 + 1 T2 for FE-ARCH-1.4) plus a new dedicated test file crates/enforcer-rules/tests/frontend_react_registry.rs (7 tests) mirroring the d16 fsm.json / fsm_registry.rs precedent exactly: each FE-* family gets its OWN standalone catalog + OWN registry test file, never merged into rules/rules.json or registry_load.rs's baseline-catalog test. This is consistent with the workpack's constraint ("must not touch the crate's Validator registration root or enforcer-rules routing beyond the FE-* rule records").
why: Confirms the standalone-catalog-per-family pattern (established by d16/d22) is the correct and only wiring path for a new rule family living inside an existing lang-pack crate; there is no central registry file that must also be touched.
howToApply: Future lang-pack rule families added inside an EXISTING crate (not a new crate) should add exactly one new rules/<family>.json catalog + one new tests/<family>_registry.rs test file in enforcer-rules, and leave registry_load.rs/rules.json untouched, exactly as d16 (fsm.json) and this lane (frontend-react.json) both did.
